newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Senate to "address" tuition hikes - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Senate to "address" tuition hikes - paper.

text.p: An aide to the New York State Senator Majority Leader told students, who were protesting Gov. George Pataki's plans to raise tuition, that their concerns would be dealt with, the Albany Times Union reported Friday.
"When you see the budget that is eventually adopted and negotiated, you will see these issues addressed," Jeffrey Lovell, Joseph Bruno's top advisor for higher education issues, told the paper.

The 18 students protested outside the office of the Senate Majority Leader, a Troy Republican, criticizing Bruno for not taking a stand to oppose Pataki's proposed budget for fiscal 1998, which calls for a $400 tuition increase, a $180 million cut to the State University of New York, a $175 million cut in tuition assistance, and changes in welfare rules that would not let work-study or college credit hours fulfill workfare requirements.
